exitCodes.meaning: success; also -h/--help, version, and a chat the person ends
the command failed: any error is printed as `sleipnir: <error>` on stderr
usage: no command, an unknown command, or an unknown or malformed flag
unfinished: a swarm's manager stopped with work left undone

flags.desc: compare | scenarios | pins | agents

flags.name: provider
flags.desc: cache model: anthropic (explicit breakpoints, 5m TTL, 1.25x writes) | marketplace (automatic prefix cache, no write premium)

flags.name: seed
flags.desc: workload seed

commands.summary: Shorthand for run --swarm: a manager and up to N workers. N counts workers and must be 1 or more.

positional.name: N
positional.desc: number of workers (1 or more; the manager comes on top)

positional.name: GOAL
positional.desc: the goal: the remaining words, or - to read stdin

flags.name: allow
flags.desc: a permission rule that needs no question in this run, repeatable: 'Bash(go test:*)', 'Edit(docs/**)'; the name tests stands for the build and test commands of most projects (go, cargo, npm, pnpm, yarn, pytest, unittest, mvn, gradle, dotnet and make: test, build, check, lint and vet, and go mod init and tidy, never install or run); more in docs/CONFIGURATION.md

flags.name: ask-timeout
flags.desc: refuse a question to the person that nobody answers within this time, and tell the worker (default: wait for the person); for a run that is left alone

flags.name: budget-usd
flags.desc: stop when spend reaches this many US dollars

flags.name: capture
flags.desc: ask the endpoint for token ids and logprobs (self-hosted policy servers; RL data)

flags.name: commit
flags.desc: swarm with --isolation worktree: commit the verified result onto your branch instead of leaving uncommitted edits (needs a clean checkout on a branch)

flags.name: context-window
flags.desc: override the model's context window (small values force frequent compaction)

flags.name: continue
flags.desc: continue this project's newest session (same as --resume latest)

flags.name: cwd
flags.desc: working directory (default: current)

flags.name: isolation
flags.desc: swarm: none | worktree (default: config swarm.isolation). worktree gives every writer a git worktree of its own; finished work is merged and verified through a queue and applied to your checkout at the end

flags.name: json
flags.desc: stream events as JSON lines on stdout

flags.name: mailman
flags.defaultNote: config swarm.mailman; --mailman=false turns it off for this run
flags.desc: swarm: route worker mail through a mailman agent that digests bursts (default: config swarm.mailman; --mailman=false turns it off for this run). Its model: --role-model mailman=<model>

flags.name: max-steps
flags.desc: step limit for a single agent

flags.name: mode
flags.desc: permissions: default | accept-edits | plan | bypass | yolo (default: config, then default)

flags.name: model
flags.desc: model: provider/model or a bare id for the default provider (default: config models.default)

flags.name: no-mcp
flags.desc: start no MCP tool servers

flags.name: no-recon
flags.desc: do not survey the project into the shared prompt layer

flags.name: no-web
flags.desc: disable the web tools

flags.name: quiet
flags.desc: print only the final answer

flags.name: resume
flags.desc: continue an earlier session, of one agent or of a team (its manager and its board): its id, its directory, or 'latest' (this project's newest)

flags.name: role-model
flags.desc: role=model override, repeatable (e.g. manager=heimdall/x)

flags.name: session-dir
flags.desc: directory for this run's recording (events.jsonl, blobs/, checkpoints/); default <state>/sessions/<id>, <state> being $SLEIPNIR_HOME or ~/.sleipnir

flags.name: trust-project
flags.desc: trust this project: apply its security-sensitive config (hooks, allow rules, providers, MCP servers) and read its AGENTS.md, skills, commands and agent definitions; only for repositories you trust

flags.name: verbose
flags.desc: print notices and tool errors

flags.name: verify
flags.desc: swarm: command the harness runs before a worker's task may leave 'doing' (with --isolation worktree, also on every merge). {dirs} in it stands for the directories the task may touch (./... without a scope), so that each task is verified on its own work: 'go test {dirs}'
